asserts: Accessibility defaults (no more contrast, reduce motion, large targets, underline links; focus ring 0; single keys on; toast 5 s) match Bulwark.
Mail CSS for the accessibility override contains underline links, 80ch measure and 0.05em letter spacing; override is active when set.
Colour-vision-deficiency mapping sends the red, orange, yellow and green inputs to the Okabe-Ito colours.
Admin task rows: label and detail split, pending state shown, DKIM rotation row built.
Cluster node rows (id, host, role, stale flag) and group summaries ("a, c", "All", "a, b, c +2").
The 11 admin actions exist, "Reload: X" labels split into group and name, and action payloads are shaped as the server expects (InvalidateCaches).
Action result lists keep warnings, scores and dotted tag keys, and drop the id field.
Attachment names split into stem and kind (report.final.pdf gives PDF); dotfiles and names without an extension have no kind.
Previewable attachments are images under the size limit; SVG and PDF are not previewed; wanted() depends on the flag.
Thumbnails are THUMB x THUMB pixels; non-image bytes give no thumbnail.
Authentication-Results parse into three entries; DKIM header.d aligns with the From domain only for a child domain.
An SPF pass counts only when smtp.mailfrom aligns with the From domain.
DMARC fail and SPF softfail count as failures; a DKIM pass suppresses an SPF softfail; dkim=none is not a failure.
domain_of lower-cases and strips the trailing dot; alignment accepts subdomains and rejects suffix look-alikes (ba.com for a.com).
Autosave is due only after 2 s of quiet and only when the draft changed since the last save or the send is queued.
Save generations: a finished save returns Send when a send was queued, and stale generations are ignored.
Reopening a draft while a save is in flight keeps the queued save and reset_leftover reports it for the right generation.
root_domain reduces a host to its registrable domain (including co.uk); valid_domain accepts ordinary hosts.
Avatar lookup order is BIMI, then Gravatar, then favicon, as in Bulwark.
No avatar is returned when avatars are off or the address is junk.
Gravatar hash is the SHA-256 of the trimmed, lower-cased address, 64 hex characters.
BIMI l= must be https; DMARC pass domain is read from Authentication-Results.
The avatar worker thread is counted out under the queue lock when idle, so the counter is zero after the queue drains.
Avatar rasters are EDGE x EDGE; a 1-pixel image is rejected.
Body cache is LRU by count: a get refreshes recency and the least recent entry is evicted first.
Entries are keyed per account; another account never sees a body.
Cache stays within 25 000 bytes by evicting oldest entries; the newest entry always stays.
Replacing an entry keeps the byte total accurate; clearing returns it to zero.
A list sync patches keywords and mailbox ids in cached bodies, keeps the body text, and drops removed messages and their threads.
Local flag changes (seen) reach cached bodies and the conversation strip; a thread that lost a message is re-read.
A fetch started before a clear is not stored afterwards (generation check).
Conversation (thread) cache is bounded by MAX_THREAD_BYTES and evicts the oldest threads.
Cache weight counts header bytes (at least 4000 more for a large header).
Cache weight counts body value text (at least 1000 bytes for a 1000-byte body).
New event data: title, start, duration (PT1H30M), time zone and the default fields are written.
Duration across a DST change is computed from wall-clock times (PT4H).
Guests, participation status of the organiser, alerts and locations are written when the event is sent.
Editing keeps participant and location ids, the RSVP answer, and fields that did not change.
The user is detected as organiser from the organiser address, owner role or isOrigin flag; case-insensitive.
Editing one occurrence, this and future, or the series produces the right patch (recurrenceOverrides keyed by occurrence start).
Free-slot finder skips busy time and off-hours; availability reports Tentative or Busy with counts.
Attendee strings parse "Name <addr>", bare addresses; malformed or dotless addresses give None.
Task markers (open and done circles) are removed from agenda titles; the task day is computed.
A feed event gets a stable UID from the feed URL and content; an existing UID is kept.
Feed events drop remote alerts and use default alerts false; import sanitising keeps local alerts.
Quick-add parses due dates from words (tomorrow, fri, monday, in 3 days) and strips them from the title.
Due labels (Today, Tomorrow, Overdue, date) and their sort rank; completed tasks have no overdue label.
Task fields map to the JMAP Task object (title, due with time zone, priority).
Birthdays from contact dates produce agenda items with age, stable ids (bday:...) and no-year variants.
Agenda time labels: a time range, All day, or until HH:MM for overnight events.
Imported events lose id, get calendarIds and an organiser address, and a zero duration is PT0S.
People search ranks names and matching calendar addresses and excludes people already invited.
Sidebar shows at most SIDEBAR_TASKS tasks with an overdue count; a task is overdue only before today and not completed.
Day columns follow the visible range (3 days, 7 days, one day).
Occurrences carry recurrence ids (event|start), durations are kept, all-day titles default, and tasks are skipped.
Namespaced ids: own-account ids stay plain; shared ids are prefixed x~id and split back.
Blurring the recipient field commits a full address but keeps partial text while suggestions are open.
Contact cards and groups become recipient sources in order; group members are listed with their addresses.
Recent recipients come from Sent, de-duplicated by address and keeping the first name.
A draft is blank only when no recipients, subject, body or user text exist; a signature alone counts as blank.
Recipients format as "Name <addr>" with quoting of commas and quotes; a bare address stays bare.
Quoted inline images become cid: references with a matching inline part carrying the blob id.
Reply picks the identity that matches a recipient (exact, +tag, domain), in a fixed order; no match gives None.
Reply window docks to the main window only when the setting, the view and the compose state allow it.
Placeholder detection finds {{ name }}, [TIME], [Your Name] and TODO markers; link text and known phrases are not placeholders.
Delivered-To headers are read as a list of addresses in order (for the reply identity).
Duplicate contacts group by name, email and normalised phone; a phone with too few digits has no key.
Merge keeps the newest contact, adds missing emails and phones from the others and keeps the VIP keyword.
vCard fields round-trip; unknown properties are kept; labels and kinds (fax, work) are preserved.
Edits add, remove and validate emails and phones; contexts and features patch correctly.
Dates display in long form and upcoming birthdays count days until the next occurrence.
Import batches assign uid and address book ids; principals are handled in batches.
Contact photos shrink to a JPEG with the aspect ratio kept (512 x 341); a non-image is an error.
A message that already has a dark-mode media query is detected (case-insensitive); light-only styles are not.
Media queries are rewritten so the app theme decides the colour scheme and the message's own queries are pinned.
The body is hidden (pending class) until the dark pass has run, then coloured with the app background; the script carries the colours.
A zero change shows 0% and is flat.
Time axis labels follow the 12/24 hour setting.
Sub-millisecond axis ticks are formatted distinctly (0.25 ms, 0.5 ms).
Start hidden only when launched at login, with the tray available and start minimised on.
Tray tooltip reads Barbican, with singular and plural unread counts.
Desktop settings rows list start-at-login, start minimised and close to tray; the update section lists check, channel and auto update.
A message already in the target mailbox is skipped when dropped there.
A drag under the threshold leaves the event unchanged.
Moving an event sends scheduling messages only when it has attendees.
Dropping a folder among siblings renumbers sortOrder for the affected siblings only.
Dropping a folder inside another sets parentId and renumbers.
Folder drop refuses cycles and moving special folders (Inbox); allowed drops are accepted.
Event drags snap to 15-minute steps and keep the duration.
Pane widths clamp to SIDE_MIN and LIST_MAX; NaN falls back to defaults.
Trash batch names encode time and batch id (time~batch) and parse back.
Trash listing names subfolders and files, and parses batch metadata.
A multi-condition filter rule builds Bulwark-shaped JSON with a bw- id and round-trips.
Rule validation: a rule needs conditions and actions, a move needs a folder, forward needs a valid address.
Rules reorder up and down; the summary line lists conditions and actions.
Sieve wildcard matching: * and ? match as in Sieve :matches.
Apply-to-existing-mail plan: supported rules become Email/query plus steps; unsupported rules are reported.
A scan result for a rule that was replaced or whose dialog closed is dropped.
Apply steps build JSON Pointer patches with ~0/~1 escaping and ifInState; Done counts applied.
An invalid regex in a rule is refused with an error.
Odd header names (X-Spam_Flag) and values with quotes or backslashes are quoted in the generated Sieve.
A search hit's folder is the open folder if it contains the message, else the inbox, else the first mailbox.
Search operators parse: from:, subject:, has:attachment, is:unread and the others.
Unknown keys, URLs, quoted phrases and foo:bar stay as free text; in:files selects files scope.
in: scope rewrites and removing a chip (from:, in:) rewrites the query text.
Free text splits into terms with quoted phrases kept; a lone wildcard gives no term.
Mail filter AND-combines the text, the operators and the mailbox; trash and junk are excluded when not chosen.
A remote (server) query is needed for contacts text, is:unread in mail, and not for empty input.
Search chips list from:, has:, is:, in: in order with their values.
Snippets mark search hits; the marked segments and markdown output escape HTML.
Snippet filter loosens terms to text, subject and phrase conditions.
Search results rank by title match: exact match first, then prefix, then word match.
File search skips trashed files and reports folder subtitle and place.
A term matches if any field contains it; empty fields never match.
Badge text: empty for 0, the number up to 99, then 99+.
The icon renders at 32 x 32 RGBA, the plain icon has a transparent corner, and a badge changes the pixels.
ICO file header: two images, 16 px entry, 256 px written as 0, correct data offset.
Writes the icon assets to disk (the extractor found no assert lines; read the body before porting).
Command-line mailto argument parsing and the single-instance request format (token line then URL).
A second launch hands its mailto to the running instance over loopback only when the token and greeting match.
A foreign program on a stale port receives nothing (no token leak).
The calendar (ICS) part is found among attachments and inline parts by type or name.
iCalendar METHOD is read from text (case, parameters); unknown METHOD maps to Unknown.
Organiser and my participant are read; an organiser who also attends can answer; organiser match is case-insensitive.
ICS durations (PT1H30M, P1DT2H, P2W) convert to seconds; bad durations give None.
Invitation trust: a spoofed organiser or an aligned pass for a different sender triggers the caution text.
Imported invitation strips id and method, sets calendarIds and uid; RSVP patch escapes the participant id.
Reschedule fallbacks: recreate the submission first when the id is known, then restore the draft.
The From header uses the identity name, or the override address when it is one of the identity's addresses.
Stalwart state codec round-trips change ids (0 to u64::MAX) and matches Bulwark's captured vectors.
A state that goes backwards (lower id) is detected; equal or opaque states are not.
Mailbox/changes or Email/changes response parses created, updated, destroyed, new state and updatedProperties; cannotCalculateChanges gives None.
Object delta merges partial updates into the cached objects by id, keeping untouched fields.
A list delta inserts new messages, removes destroyed ones, updates changed ones, and updates total and thread counts.
Additions beyond the loaded window are left to paging, and the total is kept.
A changed row is refreshed in place (keyword updated) and the total stays the same.
Calls split into batches by maxCallsInRequest unless they are linked by back-references or creation ids.
A batch is read-only only when every method is a /get, /query, /changes or similar.
Problem details: maxCallsInRequest and unknown capability messages are readable; a 500 without detail names the status.
SSE parser: state change events (per account types) and ping events are parsed in order.
Keyword validity follows RFC 8621 (no spaces, parentheses, braces, percent, quotes); $label:* is valid.
pick_quota prefers the octets quota of the mail account over others.
Address parsing keeps quoted names with commas as one address (Doe, Jane).
Delayed send is allowed only when the account has maxDelayedSend and FUTURERELEASE is advertised.
A counts-only mailbox update for a folder not yet known fetches it whole; known folders are patched.
Syncing identical rows touches nothing (untouched stats).
A changed row is set in place (one set, no insert or remove).
New mail at the top is one insert.
A deleted row is one remove.
Load more appends rows at the end (two inserts).
Mixed insert, remove, update and move result in the right final rows.
A mostly new list resets the model once instead of many edits.
A large reorder resets the model.
A filter keeping few rows resets the model.
Duplicate keys reset the model rather than corrupt it.
Syncing an empty list clears rows; syncing identical empties is untouched.
The first sync installs the model; later syncs run in place.
Nested row values compare by content, not identity.
Lite (plain-text) mode renders the email HTML at 600 px wide with a height over 900 px. Lite is dropped (D-233); the user confirms at the M1 gate.
A forced read or unread (read!, unread!) sets the state and never toggles.
Window title shows the unread count: (5) Barbican, or plain Barbican at zero.
Archive folder paths by year or month (2024, 2024/06) from the message date.
Import summary text: singular and plural message counts and already-in-folder counts.
mbox splits into messages at From lines; each message body starts at its headers.
mbox "From " envelope lines are recognised, including MAILER-DAEMON with a short time.
Imported message states (seen, flagged) become keywords; dates are read.
A single .eml is one message with its bytes preserved.
Import loop counts created, not-created and duplicate messages; each message is uploaded once.
The streaming mbox reader yields messages one at a time and caps .eml size.
mailto: parses To, Cc, Bcc and quoted names (RFC 6068).
mailto: recipient count is capped at 200 and the cap is honoured.
Registry plans for the mailto handler (HKCU Software Classes paths and command line) are built correctly. Windows registration, not run on Linux.
A moved executable is detected: the registered command no longer matches the current path.
Fragments (#) are ignored; subject is read; a pending mailto is kept until the app is ready.
Keyboard key strings for forwarded keys parse (c|k is Control+k, s|? is Shift+?).
The remote-content CSP allows inline styles and data: fonts, and blocks scripts (script-src none) when remote content is blocked.
Disposition-Notification-To addresses are extracted from the header (first address rule).
Read receipts are sent automatically only when the requester is the return path or a trusted sender; a third party is asked.
Read receipt is a two-part report with the Date, From, Message-ID and In-Reply-To headers.
Receipt headers are not injectable (no Bcc or X- headers from message content).
Base64 bodies wrap at 76 characters per line.
Requester is read from the receipt header; offer rules follow the setting.
The identity used for a receipt follows the recipient (pick_identity by to/cc).
The reduce-motion setting wins over the system setting when set (on or off).
Unread state for an opened message comes from the list copy first, then the fetched copy.
Inline image size counts as 5 MB for the inline budget.
One new message gives a toast with the sender as title and the preview as body.
Toast XML escapes ampersands, angle brackets and quotes.
A batch of several messages gives a summary toast whose activation opens the inbox.
Toast activation encodes and decodes action and context (archive, mail id).
Toast markup lists the title and text lines in order.
A token rejected after another process rotated it retries with the stored token.
A rejection with an unchanged stored token needs sign-in again.
A network error keeps the tokens and retries later (transient).
A token that changed in storage is retried with the stored value.
invalid_grant with an unchanged token needs sign-in.
Network errors are transient, not sign-in errors.
A rejection is detected from the token error text (invalid_grant, 400) and not from timeouts.
Verification codes are found in mail text (numeric and alphanumeric, German wording).
Promo codes, tracking and order numbers are not treated as verification codes.
Palette matches when every typed word matches; empty query matches all.
App commands are listed before mail commands; a command matches its group name.
Mail commands (read, reply) are offered only when a message is open.
Account switch commands are offered for other accounts only, and capability-gated commands appear only when the capability is present.
Settings pages are offered as "Go to <page> settings" commands.
The spam-score plugin DLL loads and reports its id (spam-score). Windows only; fixture under tests/fixtures.
A quick rule is refused when the Sieve script was edited by hand (no silent overwrite).
Quick rule candidates (sender addresses, domain) are read from the message.
Sieve fileinto paths for quick-rule folders (INBOX/News, Archive).
Quick-rule presets build Bulwark-shaped rules (name "Move from X to Y", domain_is condition).
Applying a quick rule creates a rule, merges into an existing one, or reports it is already covered.
Folded headers unfold; List-Unsubscribe and other headers are found case-insensitively and in multiples.
List-Unsubscribe parses HTTP and mailto targets.
Blob/copy request between accounts is built; the same account gives none.
One-click unsubscribe is trusted only when DKIM passes for the list's domain.
One-click unsubscribe refuses private and loopback addresses (SSRF guard); public IPs are allowed.
One-click unsubscribe does not follow redirects.
One-click unsubscribe POSTs the RFC 8058 form body with form-encoded content type.
Subject prefixes (Re:, Fwd:, AW:, RE[2]:) are stripped for display.
A message is shown as truncated when its body is cut; the source view cut is detected.
Files tree and FileNode objects: folder tree ordering and node shape for files.
A message/rfc822 part, or an .eml attachment, counts as a message attachment.
Internationalised domains convert to ASCII (bücher.de to xn--bcher-kva.de); ASCII addresses keep their case.
Email validation accepts plus-tags and IDN addresses.
A mailbox string splits into name and address, with or without a space before the bracket.
Recipient lists split on commas and semicolons, honouring quoted names and group syntax.
Group recipients expand into members; invalid addresses are reported.
Pasted recipient lists parse into addresses and names.
Suggestions rank groups first, then by name, with stable order.
The default suggestion is the matching index for an address, or -1 when none matches.
ISO durations (PT1H30M, P1D) convert to seconds.
Weekly rules by weekday with interval and count generate the expected dates.
UNTIL is inclusive; the start counts as the first occurrence.
Monthly nth weekday rules (3rd Thursday, last weekday) generate the right dates.
A monthly rule on day 31 skips months without a 31st.
Yearly rules on a given month and day generate the right dates.
Overrides, excluded occurrences and moved occurrences are applied.
Rule summaries read naturally (weekly every 2 weeks on Wednesday; monthly on the 3rd Thursday).
A rule round-trips through JSON and two rules are the same when their content is.
Occurrences before a split point are counted, so COUNT is adjusted for the remaining series.
Local times convert across time zones (incl. America/New_York) and back.
Release asset file names map to manifest keys (windows-x86_64-msi, windows-x86_64-zip).
MSI version numbers encode prerelease ordering (1.2.0 gives 1.2.999; beta gives a lower number).
Manifest freshness fields: published and expires (published + VALID_SECS).
A stable release is offered on the beta channel; decide() returns the right result.
A manifest built by the release tool verifies in the updater (hash and version).
Fetch-ahead window is 8 days by default and 15 days when calendars use longer default alerts.
Alert offsets parse (-PT15M gives -900 000 ms) and convert to a unit and amount.
An event's own alerts override the calendar defaults.
An alerts patch keeps unchanged alerts and is empty when nothing changed.
Due alerts for a series and tasks fire at the computed time.
Missed reminders are shown once within the missed window and acknowledged ones are not repeated.
Schedule presets (This morning, Tomorrow afternoon) give the right local times.
Schedule date and time parsing accepts ISO and dotted dates and 12-hour times.
Scheduled-send labels show the day, time and 12-hour form when the setting asks for it.
Search history keeps the newest first and drops duplicates (case-insensitive).
Suggestions combine recent searches and fill up to five entries, as Bulwark does.
People suggestions match name or address (case-insensitive, by domain too).
Settings export, import and reset round-trip the values (theme dark, showPreview false).
Mail keys never flip the read state by themselves; Backspace passes through and does not delete.
The palette (k) and help (?) work in every place.
With single keys off, letter and ? keys pass through; named keys still work.
g then i goes to the inbox (sequence arming).
Mail keys: arrows move the selection, Shift+arrows extend it, K moves up.
Composer keys: Ctrl+Shift+C shows Cc, Ctrl+Shift+B shows Bcc.
Calendar keys: right arrow goes to next, t goes to today.
List keys: arrows move, Home jumps to the first item.
Stepping through a list wraps and starts at the first item when nothing is selected.
Help rows split alternatives (j / down arrow).
Single-key detection: letters and ? are single keys.
Hand-written Sieve blocks (elsif, else, text: strings with a leading #) are kept verbatim in the external part.
A vacation-only script parses into metadata and has no external part and is not locked.
Hand-written blocks between generated ones survive regeneration.
The generated script has the Bulwark metadata comment and require line (round-trip shape).
Active-period tests (activeFrom, activeUntil) generate the Bulwark date tests; bad values are rejected.
A rule with an active period generates the Bulwark allof form with a mailbox fileinto.
Vacation audience and forwarding generate Bulwark-shaped spamtest and forward blocks.
Scripts with an unknown version or extras, or bad rule dates, stay locked (not rewritten).
Form dates become UTC day boundaries (ending in .000Z).
Tag ids are normalised like Bulwark (lower case, spaces and slashes become dashes).
Generated tag ids use the same FNV hash as the JavaScript client.
Tag tree rows carry depth and child counts in order.
Adding a tag under a parent gives the nested id (work/clients).
Stored tag definitions and colours parse; defaults apply when none are stored.
Template deletion writes a tombstone and keeps other deleted tombstones (version 1).
The unread badge sums the other logins for an account (4 for a, 7 when none match).
Unified inbox merges messages from several accounts ordered by parsed time and removes duplicates.
Row ids keep messages from different sources apart (own versus shared).
Unified fetch reads each account once even when it is shared.
Positions count per source account (for paging).
Shared accounts are read from the session; source keys combine user and group.
Mailbox matching by role first, then by name (archive, receipts).
Version comparison: 1.2.0 is newer than 1.1.9 and newer than its own beta.
Update decision: MSI installs automatically on stable; .deb only notifies.
Install kind is detected from the executable path (AppImage mount, /usr/bin is deb).
A signed manifest verifies and yields the version and notes URL.
Feed URL templates substitute the channel; a bare feed gets channel.json.
At start, a pending update is applied or nothing is done, depending on the pending record.
Pending update record round-trips to disk and the file replacement writes new bytes.
The MSI install command runs PowerShell with the install script as last argument.
A pending update path is accepted only inside the update directory with the right extension.
A manifest is fresh until its expiry; an expired manifest is rejected.
Download file names follow the pattern barbican-<version>.<ext>; AppImage keeps its name.
A download is accepted only when its SHA-256 matches; a partial file is removed on failure.
Download size limits are enforced (declared and actual size).
vCard 3 parses with types and Apple labels; the full name keeps prefix and suffix.
Reduced vCard dates (--0412 without year) parse with month and day only.
vCard round-trips with UID, typed EMAIL and line folding at 75 octets.
Quoted-printable values decode (Jürgen); empty cards are skipped.
Duplicates within the file and against existing contacts are detected; data URIs parse.
Attachment names in a zip are unique (a.pdf, a (1).pdf, a (2).pdf).
The zip writer produces a readable central directory (EOCD signature, two entries).
Hunspell protocol answers parse: * and + are OK, & and # are suggestions and misses.
Misspelt words are located in UTF-16 offsets (emoji counted as two units).
Dictionary names map from locale tags (de-DE to de_DE).
Portal colour-scheme reply parses to dark (1) or light (2). Linux only.
gsettings colour-scheme reply parses to dark or light. Linux only.
Autostart entries (name Barbican, command with --autostart) are planned correctly.
Config and data folders end in Barbican (Windows) or barbican (Linux).
Registry reads return None for a missing value and do not write.
Typing groups edits for undo; undo reverts the group.
Markdown block shortcuts (# for heading) convert the paragraph into a heading.
Markdown inline shortcuts (**bold**) apply bold and remove the markers.
Toggling bold applies to the selection and to the caret for typing.
List items indent and backspace outdents.
Links add a link mark to the run and the current link is read back.
Tables create cells; Tab moves between cells.
Inserting an image keeps the following text (quoted text stays after the image).
Replacing the draft text keeps the quoted block.
Image resize keeps the aspect ratio when asked; replace-range edits the blocks.
HTML import maps strong and em to bold and italic runs.
HTML import maps headings, paragraphs, lists (bullet and numbered) and quotes to blocks.
HTML tables import as cells with header detection.
HTML whitespace collapses and entities decode (&).
HTML export and import round-trip the marks, blocks and indents.
Plain-text export: links as <url>, lists with markers, quotes with >.
HTML export escapes text (< > & and nbsp).
Quoted reply blocks round-trip and the attribution line stays.
Quote cleaning removes the quoted tail and leaves the reply text.
The HTML source view round-trips and puts one block per line; the quote stays out of the source view.
Editing the source keeps inline image cid references.
Image width survives export (width attribute and style).
Inserting text into a run merges adjacent runs with equal marks.
Splitting and merging blocks keeps text in the right blocks and returns the new position.
Enter at the end of a heading creates a paragraph.
Ordered-list numbering counts per level.
Pasting several blocks splits and merges text correctly.
Deleting inside a table keeps the table's cell grid.
Marks at a caret position are read from the adjacent run.
Spell-check language tags map (de to de-DE; auto uses the system tag).
UTF-16 ranges convert to byte ranges, including emoji.
URLs and e-mail addresses are skipped by the spell checker.
Windows spell checker finds misspelt words (sentense, mispelled). Windows only.
